name: window-colors
description: Gives every VS Code window its own color, also windows with no folder or workspace open.

windowColors.stripeWidth.markdownDescription: Width in pixels of the colored stripe on the left of every editor (and the matching mark in the scrollbar). `0` turns the stripe off.

windowColors.tintFolderWindows.markdownDescription: In windows with a folder or workspace open, color the window border, title bar, activity bar and status bar by writing `workbench.colorCustomizations` into that folder's `.vscode/settings.json` (like Peacock), replacing colors a folder still has from Peacock.

windowColors.tintEmptyWindows.markdownDescription: In windows with no folder open, color the window border, title bar, activity bar and status bar too. VS Code has no per-window settings, so this writes `workbench.colorCustomizations` into your user settings whenever such a window gets focus: folder windows keep their own colors, but other open windows without a folder show the color of the one focused last.

windowColors.palette.markdownDescription: Colors handed out to new windows, as `#rrggbb`. Empty uses the built-in ten.
